title: Pre-Analysis — Harness Segregation Standard Against the Later Bay Work

ata.title: Forward Fuselage Wiring — Avionics Bay Harnesses

abstract: Closed work order asking what the harness segregation standard commits for any later work at the same feedthrough, rejected as premature when no later work was found to be defined.

sections.objective: Establish what the avionics bay harness segregation standard commits for future work at the same feedthrough, so that a later modification does not undo it. The work order was raised speculatively by the wiring design office rather than against a specific proposal.
sections.findings_summary: The commitment is real but there was nothing to commit it against. The segregation standard fixes which aperture carries which route and where the screen terminates, and any later work that opens the feedthrough has to respect both. The routing check task states this correctly and even instructs the technician not to re-route a harness on a single-aperture feedthrough to improve separation, which is the right instruction and is easy to get wrong. What the work order could not do was identify a later change to constrain, because none was defined at the time. Raising a pre-analysis against a hypothetical is not a good use of the process, and the work order was rejected on that basis rather than on anything found. The wiring sheet is the durable record and it already carries both feedthrough standards with their separate screen termination points.
sections.next_steps: Reject the work order as premature. Record the commitment in the wiring sheet, which already carries it, rather than in a work order. Re-raise against a specific proposal if one appears.

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to the wiring sheet it impacts.

expected_findings.rationale: The wiring sheet carries both feedthrough standards with their separate screen termination points and support dimensions. It is the durable record of the commitment and needs nothing added.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the harness and clamp part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The routing check task instructs the technician not to improve separation by re-routing on a single-aperture feedthrough, which is the correct instruction and the one most likely to be ignored by a well-meaning engineer.
expected_findings.resolution: No action; noted as a good example of an instruction that needs its reason stated.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and rejected as premature. Nothing was found to constrain because nothing was defined.
